```{r, include = FALSE}
                 'packages.bib')
```

<img src="images/cover.jpg" class="cover" width="250" height="328"/> This is the second book in the Data Analysis series. Like its companion, it is an effort to simplify and demystify data analysis, making it accessible to a wide audience. Writing it has been as much a learning journey for me as I hope it will be for you.

The first book, [*A Guide on Data Analysis*](https://mike-data-analysis.share.connect.posit.cloud/), is concerned with interpretation and causal inference: understanding *why*, and estimating effects we can defend. This book turns to the other half of the discipline, prediction. The principles and philosophy are the same; the goal is different.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

This book differs from the [first one](https://mike-data-analysis.share.connect.posit.cloud/) in emphasis: it is about building models that predict well, whereas the first book is about interpreting relationships and defending causal claims. The opening chapters develop that distinction (prediction versus estimation) in full; the preface only needs to flag it.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## How to cite this book {.unnumbered}

This is the open online edition. If you reference it, please also consider citing the companion volume, [*Foundations of Data Analysis*](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-032-01858-8) (Springer Cham, 2025).

1. APA (7th edition)

Nguyen, M. *Advanced data analysis*. Retrieved from [https://advanced-data-analysis.netlify.app/](https://advanced-data-analysis.netlify.app/)

2. MLA (8th edition)

Nguyen, Mike. *Advanced Data Analysis*. [https://advanced-data-analysis.netlify.app/](https://advanced-data-analysis.netlify.app/).

3. Chicago (17th edition)

Nguyen, Mike. *Advanced Data Analysis*. [https://advanced-data-analysis.netlify.app/](https://advanced-data-analysis.netlify.app/).

4. Harvard

Nguyen, M. *Advanced Data Analysis*. Available at: [https://advanced-data-analysis.netlify.app/](https://advanced-data-analysis.netlify.app/)

```bibtex
@book{Nguyen_AdvancedDataAnalysis,
  author = {Nguyen, Mike},
  title  = {Advanced Data Analysis},
  url    = {https://advanced-data-analysis.netlify.app/}
}
```

## Use this book in your AI assistant {.unnumbered}

This book is indexed by the [Research Methods Library](https://research-methods-mcp.vercel.app/), a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that makes it available to AI assistants. Given a research question, an assistant connected to the server recommends candidate study designs, states their identifying assumptions, returns runnable R and Python code, and cites the sections of this book and of the author's other works on which each answer draws. Access is free and requires no account or API key.

**Endpoint:** `https://research-methods-mcp.vercel.app/mcp`

- **Claude** (web, desktop, and mobile): Settings → Connectors → **Add custom connector**; enter the endpoint.
- **Claude Code:** `claude mcp add --transport http research-methods https://research-methods-mcp.vercel.app/mcp`
- **ChatGPT:** Settings → enable developer mode → add a custom connector of type MCP server with the endpoint and no authentication.
- **Cursor** and **Visual Studio Code:** [Add to Cursor](https://cursor.com/en/install-mcp?name=research-methods&config=eyJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL3Jlc2VhcmNoLW1ldGhvZHMtbWNwLnZlcmNlbC5hcHAvbWNwIn0%3D) or [Install in VS Code](https://insiders.vscode.dev/redirect/mcp/install?name=research-methods&config=%7B%22type%22%3A%22http%22%2C%22url%22%3A%22https%3A%2F%2Fresearch-methods-mcp.vercel.app%2Fmcp%22%7D).

Configuration for other MCP clients is described on the [server's website](https://research-methods-mcp.vercel.app/).
:::

## Code Replication {.unnumbered}

This book was built with `r R.version.string` and the following packages:

```{r, echo = FALSE, results="asis", eval = FALSE}
# if you want to make it beautiful for markdown
deps <- desc::desc_get_deps()
pkgs <- sort(deps$package[deps$type == "Imports"])
pkgs <- sessioninfo::package_info(pkgs, dependencies = FALSE)
df <- tibble::tibble(
  package = pkgs$package,
  version = pkgs$ondiskversion,
  source = gsub("@", "\\\\@", pkgs$source)
)
knitr::kable(df, format = "markdown")
```

<br>

```{r, echo = FALSE}
devtools::session_info()
```
